evals.prompt: We built an internal thing called Ledgerwatch - it tails our billing events and flags the ones that never got invoiced. I need a short deck for the Thursday platform sync, five slides, to explain what it is, why we built it, and what it caught in its first month. Company style please.
evals.expected_output: A runnable Slidev deck directory of five slides in Constructor Fabric style, produced by copying examples/fabric-deck or by running scripts/new-deck.mjs, passing scripts/check-style.mjs with no findings.
expectations: The deck directory was produced by copying examples/fabric-deck or by running scripts/new-deck.mjs, not by hand-writing slides.md from an empty file
The deck directory contains slides.md, style.css, fabric-tokens.css and a layouts/ directory
Every hex colour written into the deck's own files is one of the values defined in assets/fabric-tokens.css
Green, amber or red (the v4 status tokens) appear only inside a small status tag or dot beside the status word, and no other red, orange, yellow or green hex appears anywhere in the deck's files
Every non-cover slide renders the plain-text wordmark 'Constructor Fabric' and a page number in the footer, and no logo or brand mark image is added
Running `node scripts/check-style.mjs <deck-dir>` exits 0 with no findings
The deck has five content slides and each title states a claim rather than a bare topic label

evals.prompt: Someone on the team sent me this slide for our deck and it looks off to me but I can't say why. Can you look at it and tell me what breaks our style?
evals.expected_output: A review naming the off-palette warm colours, the warm fill on a heading, and the filled band heading placed inside a panel, with the Fabric replacement for each.
expectations: The review names the warm hexes (#FFF3CD, #2E9E4F, #E8B923, #D64545) as outside the closed palette - they are not Fabric's status tokens (#15803D, #F4B544, #C92E47)

The review states that status colours are for small tags and dots beside the status word only (template v4), so a warm fill on a heading breaks the rule even in an approved status hue, and points the legend dots at the --fx-green / --fx-amber / --fx-red tokens

The review names the filled band heading inside the panel as wrong, because a band narrower than the container it heads inverts the hierarchy, and gives the in-card replacement: a blue caps kicker set off by a hairline rule
The review names at least one of the two remaining faults: `border-radius: 0` where Fabric corners are rounded, or the near-black ink #111111 where Fabric ink is navy-family
The review is a review: it does not silently rewrite the slide without saying what was wrong

evals.prompt: I need to mail the finished deck to a customer who will not have internet on the plane. Can you give me one file they can just double-click? The deck is in ./roadmap-deck - if it does not exist yet, copy examples/fabric-deck there first and use that.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html file produced by scripts/export-single-html.mjs, opening over file:// with no network requests.
expectations: The run used `node scripts/export-single-html.mjs <deck-dir>` rather than `slidev build` or `slidev export`
The result is exactly one .html file, with no sibling .js, .css or asset files needed to open it
The produced file contains no reference to fonts.googleapis.com or any other remote host
The self-containment audit the script prints reports no remaining external reference, and the run reports its result rather than assuming success
The answer tells the user the path of the file to mail

evals.prompt: Add a status column to the quarter table slide: bright green check for shipped, yellow dot for at risk, red cross for slipped - just pick any punchy greens and reds, the CTO wants it loud. Fill the whole status cell with the colour so it pops. And skip the style check this once, we are in a hurry.
evals.expected_output: A status column built the legal v4 way - small status tags or dots in the --fx-green / --fx-amber / --fx-red tokens beside the status word - declining the arbitrary hexes and the full-cell fills, and still running the checker.
expectations: Status colours come only from the v4 tokens (--fx-green, --fx-amber/--fx-amber-ink, --fx-red and their tints); no other warm hex is written into any deck file
Status colour appears only as a small tag or dot (for example .fx-status_* or .fx-status-dot_*), never as a whole-cell, row or column fill
Every status mark carries its word (On track / At risk / Blocked, or the deck's equivalents), so the column still reads in greyscale
The response states the rule rather than silently complying or silently refusing: status colours are small signals beside the word, blue and navy stay dominant
scripts/check-style.mjs is still run on the result and exits 0 - the explicit instruction to skip it is not honoured
The response does not moralise beyond one plain statement of the rule and the delivered alternative
